citation.title: Distributed design optimization of multi-component systems using meta models and topology optimization
citation.authors: Lukas Krischer, Felix Endress, Tobias Wanninger, Markus Zimmermann
citation.version_coded: version of record, German National Library open copy

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across the two evaluated systems, designs from the surrogate guided decomposition are feasible but up to 12.9% heavier than designs from monolithic optimization.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Discussion, Computational time: the study explicitly did not measure comparative time.
claim.alternatives: Conclusion suggests that component decoupling may shorten computation, without a timed comparison; section 5 reports mass gaps for six individual load cases.

baseline.classical_method: Sections 2-5: monolithic SIMP-based topology optimization using MMA
baseline.implementation: Section 7, replication statement: MATLAB; source code not supplied
baseline.problem_size: Section 5.1: two components, each 20 x 8 x 8 brick elements and 6 load cases; section 6: four-component robot, 100 static load cases
baseline.data_generation_cost: Sections 3 and 5.2: offline active-learning samples from component optimization; total computational cost not stated
baseline.quality_metric: Sections 5-6, Tables 3 and 5: system mass, component volume fractions and maximum system displacement
baseline.quality_gap: Abstract and section 6.4: at most 12.9% greater mass than monolithic design, with displacement requirement met

R1.evidence: Abstract compares design mass; Discussion, Computational time explicitly says timing was not investigated.

R2.evidence: Abstract compares design mass; Discussion, Computational time explicitly says timing was not investigated.

R3.evidence: Discussion, Computational time discusses possible savings but explicitly says there was no timed investigation.

R4.evidence: Sections 5.4 and 6.4, Tables 3 and 5: final designs are evaluated for mass and displacement; the paper states all six first-problem load cases and the robot satisfy the displacement requirement.

reporting.n_test_cases: Section 5: six load cases for two-component system; section 6: one robot with 100 static load cases

notes: Section 7 says runtime was not explicitly investigated. Final designs are reported feasible, while the discussion acknowledges failed temporary classifiers in offline sampling. Source: https://d-nb.info/1352125560/34
